description: The developer's projects: account → projects → apps. Every account has the project «Explorer» (it can be renamed, not deleted) and new apps land there; a developer who never creates another sees nothing new. The FREE quota is the account's: one pool of credits a day, store and files shared by every app of its free projects (making empty apps does not multiply it), and each app may carry a cap of its own inside the pool (set_app_caps). Pro and the quota packs are the PROJECT's (neblla_billing with projectId): a Pro project has its own pool and its apps stop drawing from the account's. Example: the chess spends 1500 credits a day of «Ajedrez»'s Pro and the free pool stays whole for the yoga and the tests. Connections: Stripe (who the apps sell as), Cloudflare (one token for the developer's server boxes, neblla_byos) and the database (where the apps keep their users' data, as neblla_byodb) are set once on the ACCOUNT, which Explorer uses, and a project may put its own and inherit the rest (example: «Ajedrez» sells with another Stripe and keeps the account's Cloudflare). Omit projectId to act on the account's. Actions: "list" (projects, their apps, plan, pool and connections, with where each comes from: project or account); "create" { name }; "rename" { projectId, name }; "delete" { projectId } (empty and not Pro); "move" { appId, projectId, confirm? }: a real move — the quota counts in the new project from now, the data moves when the two use different databases (ALL its users' data: it answers confirmRequired with the plan first; call again with confirm: true once the developer agreed), its server box redeploys on the new Cloudflare, its media follow. To a project with another Stripe, an app that sells moves too (the plan's stripe.selling says what it sells): its products wait hidden until that Stripe takes money and then publish by themselves (stripe.productsWaiting), and its live subscriptions keep charging on the Stripe they were born on until each customer cancels (stripe.subscriptionsStay), while the new ones go to the new Stripe; Neblla cancels nothing (a developer who prefers to cut cancels them by hand and tells their users). Pro stays with its project. "set_app_caps" { appId, credits?, store? (bytes), files? }: the app's own caps inside its pool; null or 0 removes one. Cloudflare, by TOPICS (C244), each optional and the developer's to choose: "media" (Fotos y archivos: their own R2 bucket for the media; free up to 10 GB but Cloudflare asks for a card), "domain" (Tu dominio: the DNS of their domain on their Cloudflare, free; buying or transferring the registration ~10 $/year, billed by Cloudflare: neblla_domains), "mail" (Correo de tu dominio: forwarding, free, no card: neblla_domains), "server" (Tu servidor: the app's box on their Workers, neblla_byos); "web" is included (Neblla serves it). "cloudflare_setup" { projectId? }: every topic with its steps (account, token rights, R2 turned on) and what is done, the Cloudflare link that creates the token already filled (tokenLink.url; tokenLink.manual: rights to add by hand on the same form), the sign-up link, and panelUrl. THE TOKEN IS NEVER PASTED IN THE CHAT: give the developer panelUrl, where they paste it in a box; never ask for it. "cloudflare_topic" { projectId?, topic, on? }: the developer wants that topic (on: false, not any more); answers the steps again, and what started (media: the buckets once its steps are done; the apps' media then move there by themselves). "cloudflare_check" { projectId? }: check the token's rights and R2 again (after the developer turned R2 on or widened the token). "connect_cloudflare": the same as cloudflare_setup (the token goes in the panel). "remove_cloudflare" { projectId?, force? }: forget the token; refused while media live in their bucket unless force (they stay there, served, no longer managed). "connect_db" { projectId?, engine, config, migrate? } / "remove_db" { projectId? }: validated now, sealed at rest; with migrate: true each app it reaches starts moving its data there (ALL its users' data: only when the developer asked). Each app keeps its tables under its own prefix, so several apps share one database. "use_own_stripe" { projectId }: the project sells with a payout account of its own; neblla_payments_account with projectId opens its onboarding. "use_account_stripe" { projectId }: back to the account's. Either way what its apps sold stays on the Stripe it was sold on (live subscriptions renew there until each customer cancels) and their products wait hidden until the new one takes money.

config.description: connect_db: { uri, dbName? } (mongo), { url, authToken } (turso), { uri } (postgres, mysql)

confirm.description: move: true once the developer agreed to move the app's data

force.description: remove_cloudflare: even with media in their bucket

migrate.description: connect_db: start moving the apps' data there now

projectId.description: The project (list gives the ids). Omitted in connect_*/remove_*: the account's.
